chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever eats watercress at night, the vein of leprosy will strike him from his nose, and he will spend the night with blood flowing.

key_terms.يُنْزَفُ: Flowing (like blood from a wound or due to intoxication)

ai.seo_question: What are the benefits or risks of eating watercress at night according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the nocturnal consumption of watercress to specific physiological and spiritual ailments, notably the 'vein of leprosy' (‘irq al-judham) manifesting in the nose and a state of 'intoxication' (nunzifu) which may denote either physical drowsiness or spiritual heedlessness. This reflects the Shia tradition of combining empirical observation with metaphysical consequences, where timing (night) alters the substance's effect on the body's humors and soul.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who eats the watercress at night, the vein of leprosy would hit him from his nose, and he would sleep with blood flowing’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If one eats watercress during the night the vein of leprosy will hit him from his nose and blood will flow thereof.”’
